description: revocation of v01 signed by an address that is neither v01's principal nor its agent; verifier MUST reject with E_REVOKER_UNAUTHORIZED per SPEC §9.5 / §8.1 revocation lookup

expected.rejection_reason: Only v01's principal (bc1qprincipal…) and its agent (bc1qagent…) may revoke it. This revocation envelope is signed by a third address (bc1qother…). Conformant verifiers MUST treat this revocation as having no protocol force — i.e., when computing whether v01 is revoked at any later action's signed_at, this revocation event MUST be ignored and §8.1 step 7 returns E_REVOKED only if some other authorized revocation predates the action.

harness_assertion: Independent of canonical-message hashing or BIP-322 signature validity, the authorization rule fires first: a revocation by a third party is rejected with E_REVOKER_UNAUTHORIZED before any other check the verifier might perform on the revocation envelope itself. Implementations that evaluate canonical-message / signature first MAY surface E_BAD_SIG or E_MALFORMED if those conditions also hold, but for a structurally-valid envelope from the wrong signer the canonical answer is E_REVOKER_UNAUTHORIZED.
